name: MathlibAnnex.PluckerBody.eq_of_sphereIsometry
title: Sphere isometries preserve the Plücker body

content.display_title: Sphere isometries preserve the Plücker body
content.one_sentence_role: Combines generator transport and its inverse for every finite output dimension.
content.natural_language_statement:
Let $m,N\in\mathbb N_0$, put $n=m+1>0$, and give $E=\mathbb R^n$ and $F=\mathbb R^N$ their coordinate sup norms. Let $\lambda_n$ be the fixed coordinate Lebesgue measure on $E$. Let $p,q:E\to\mathbb R$ be continuous real seminorms with specified positive constants $a_p,b_p,a_q,b_q$ such that
$$a_p\|x\|_\infty\le p(x)\le b_p\|x\|_\infty,\qquad a_q\|x\|_\infty\le q(x)\le b_q\|x\|_\infty\quad(x\in E).$$

Both $p$ and $q$ are norms. For each $s\in\{p,q\}$ define the closed unit ball, unit sphere, and real reference volume by
$$K_s=\{x:s(x)\le1\},\qquad\Sigma_s=\{x:s(x)=1\},\qquad v_s=\lambda_n(K_s)\in(0,\infty).$$
The finite measure is read as a real number when used as a scalar.

Let $\mathcal I_{n,N}$ be the finite set of increasing $n$-tuples of distinct rows from $\{1,\ldots,N\}$. The minor-coordinate space $\mathbb R^{\mathcal I_{n,N}}$ carries its sup norm. For a linear map $B:E\to F$, put $B_{ij}=(Be_j)_i$ in the standard coordinate basis. Write $\Pi_n(B)$ for its maximal-minor vector and $\mathcal V_p(B),\mathcal V_q(B)$ for its two volume-scaled versions. Their coordinates and scaling are
$$\Pi_n(B)_I=\det(B_{i_a,j})_{a,j=1}^n,\qquad\mathcal V_s(B)=v_s\Pi_n(B)\ (s\in\{p,q\})\quad(I=(i_1<\cdots<i_n)).$$

For each $s\in\{p,q\}$, let $\mathcal C_s^N$ consist of linear maps $B:E\to F$ with $\|Bz\|_\infty\le s(z)$ for all $z$. Set
$$\mathcal G_s^N=\{\pm\mathcal V_s(B):B\in\mathcal C_s^N\},\qquad\mathcal P_s^N=\operatorname{conv}_{\mathbb R}(\mathcal G_s^N).$$
If $\Delta:\Sigma_p\to\Sigma_q$ is a bijection with $q(\Delta(u)-\Delta(v))=p(u-v)$ for all $u,v\in\Sigma_p$, then
$$\mathcal P_p^N=\mathcal P_q^N.$$
content.assumptions: The source dimension is positive, $n=m+1$. Both seminorms have the specified positive norm comparisons and are continuous. The sphere map is a bijective chord-distance isometry. The output dimension $N$ is arbitrary, including zero.
content.conclusion: The two bodies agree for each finite $N$. This statement does not classify the norms or assert that the given sphere map itself has a linear extension.
content.proof_summary: Transport both signs, take convex hulls, and repeat for the inverse isometry.

proof_steps.text:
**Place every signed target generator in the source body.** For each $B\in\mathcal C_q^N$,
$$\mathcal V_q(B)\in\mathcal P_p^N,\qquad-\mathcal V_q(B)\in\mathcal P_p^N.$$
The first membership is [generator transport through the sphere isometry](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Plucker/BodyInvariance.lean#L134-L168) applied to $\Delta$ and this $q$-contraction $B$. The second is [sign symmetry of the same source body](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Convex/PluckerBody.lean#L41-L50). Consequently,
$$\mathcal G_q^N\subseteq\mathcal P_p^N.$$
This is [the signed-generator inclusion](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Plucker/BodyInvariance.lean#L170-L177).

**Pass to convex hulls.** Since $\mathcal P_p^N$ is convex, the preceding inclusion implies
$$\mathcal P_q^N=\operatorname{conv}_{\mathbb R}(\mathcal G_q^N)\subseteq\mathcal P_p^N.$$
Equivalently, every finite convex combination of its generators stays in the source body. This is [the body inclusion](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Plucker/BodyInvariance.lean#L179-L185).

**Use the inverse isometry for the reverse inclusion.** The bijection $\Delta^{-1}:\Sigma_q\to\Sigma_p$ satisfies the same chord-distance condition with $p,q$ interchanged. Applying Steps 1–2 to that map gives
$$\mathcal P_p^N\subseteq\mathcal P_q^N.$$
The two inclusions are for the same output dimension $N$ and the same reference minor coordinates, so they yield the asserted equality.
